                    1          Plaintiff Google LLC (“Google”), by and through its attorneys of record, brings this action
                    2   against Defendants Proloy Pondit and Does 1–20 for (1) violation of California’s Unfair
                    3   Competition Law (“UCL”), Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 17200 et seq.; (2) breach of contract; and (3)
                    4   inducement of contractual breach in violation of California law. Google alleges as follows:
                    5          1.      This action seeks to stop Defendants’ multinational scheme to sell and post fake
                    6   reviews for business listings on Google’s services such as Google Maps. Working until recently
                    7   through their website BigBoostUp.com, Defendants claim that they can and will author positive or
                    8   negative reviews for any business listed on Google Maps, virtually anywhere in the world.
                    9   Defendants provide these “services” for businesses they have never visited, instead posting
                   10   fraudulent and misleading reviews for financial gain and at the cost of both businesses and
                   11   consumers who rely on reviews.
                   12          2.      Defendants also offer to sell and post fraudulent reviews on websites run by other
                   13   companies, including Amazon.com, Inc. and Amazon.com Services LLC (together, “Amazon”),
                   14   which operates the Amazon.com store. Amazon is simultaneously bringing a parallel lawsuit
                   15   against Defendants in the Western District of Washington arising from Defendants’ posting of fake
                   16   reviews on pages for products sold on the Amazon.com store. Amazon and Google are bringing
                   17   these parallel lawsuits to prevent Defendants from selling and publishing fake reviews and other
                   18   fake content targeting Google, Amazon, and other legitimate companies and organizations—and
                   19   the members of the public who those reviews seek to deceive.
                   20          3.      Google Maps provides (among other things) detailed public listings of local
                   21   businesses with accompanying ratings and reviews submitted by Google Maps users. The
                   22   authenticity of these reviews is essential to businesses, their customers, and Google. Online ratings
                   23   and reviews, such as those found on Google Maps, play a crucial role in influencing the decisions
                   24   of numerous potential customers when they are searching for businesses to engage with.
                   25   Accordingly, these ratings and reviews must offer genuine, accurate, and truthful information about
                   26   a company’s products and services.
                   27          4.      For these reasons, Google employs numerous methods to prevent and remove fake
                   28   or otherwise inappropriate reviews on Google Maps. As part of these initiatives, Google has

                    4          5.      Defendants’ conduct harms consumers by giving them fake information about
                    5   businesses and obscuring genuine reviews. Internet users rely on Google Maps and other Google

                   11                                     FACTUAL BACKGROUND
                   12                                    GOOGLE MAPS & REVIEWS
                   13          15.     Google is a well-known provider of an Internet search engine and other online
                   14   services. One such service is Google Maps, which is free to use and has over one billion monthly
                   15   active users. Google Maps displays not only traditional map features like streets and topography,
                   16   but also clickable profile pages detailing information about businesses, service providers, and other
                   17   places of interest. These pages, known as “local listings,” span an enormous variety of businesses
                   18   and professionals around the United States and the world. These include, just to name a few,
                   19   restaurants, car mechanics, accountants, museums, dentists, hair salons, airports, law firms,
                   20   government agencies, retail stores, and amusement parks. Local listings are search results that
                   21   appear on Google products, like the Google Maps mobile application and in Google search. New
                   22   local listings may be created by businesses themselves, automatically created by Google, or
                   23   suggested by members of the public.
                   24          16.     Businesses can sign up for a Business Profile, a Google service that offers them a
                   25   suite of tools to manage their business’s local listing on Google. To create a new Business Profile
                   26   or claim an existing local listing as a Business Profile, a user must accept both Google’s Terms of
                   27   Service and the Google Business Profile Additional Terms of Service for Business Entities
                   28   (“Google Business Profile TOS”).

                    7          23.     Defendants seek to exploit customers’ reliance on reviews when making important

                   10            48.    Google makes clear to all users that there are specific rules for user-contributed
                   11   content, such as reviews on Google Maps. Most importantly, in this case, Google’s contract with
                   12   its users mandates that the reviews must be genuine and should accurately represent a user’s real
                   13   experience with a business.
                   14            49.    When a user signs up for a Google account—a prerequisite for using the Business
                   15   Profile service and for posting reviews on Google Maps—he or she must expressly agree to the
                   16   Google Terms of Service (“TOS”). 2
                   17            50.    The TOS govern users’ relationship with Google, permitting them to use Google’s
                   18   services in exchange for following certain rules and guidelines. The TOS incorporate by reference
                   19   various “service-specific additional terms” that apply to individual Google products, including
                   20   Maps, such as the Maps User Contributed Content Policy.
                   21            51.    At all relevant times, the TOS and the Maps User Contributed Content Policy have
                   22   included requirements for “Maps user contributed content to help ensure everyone viewing user
                   23   generated content has a positive, beneficial experience.” They provide that contributions must be
                   24   “based on real experiences and information,” and they prohibit “[d]eliberately fake content” and
                   25   “incorrect content.” These policies reflect that Google “go[es] to great lengths to make sure content
                   26   published by third-party contributors is useful and reflects the world [its] users explore.” 3
